security_privacy_cost_impact: Security: assertion and tooling only; no grant, policy, role or schema changes. Each closure refuses a later migration that weakens an unread guarantee, none reachable by a client on the clean set: a trigger on any app or private table (A1 R-2, the lifecycle_state writer among them), a schema owner or a non-client role attribute changed (A1 S1, S3; Q0 R-2), an index whose collation or operator class does not serve its predicate (Q0 R-2), a COPY ... PROGRAM in a migration (a server shell command, C0 G1), and test-reach gaps in the static suites. Redaction now covers a fragment-carried host (G-2). Cost: the pinned grant probe runs two more drift jobs (eight in all); migrate-clean stays about 5 s of probe time on this host.
migration_and_data_impact: None. No migration file is added or edited. Two lint files change one _how_measured line each (regenerated on the clean set), and the retention and audit coverage maps change only their blocker citations (line numbers to quotes).
compatibility_impact: Tests stay 684 (none added or renamed); foundation-contract's assertion floor 946 -> 1000 and identity-isolation's 2167 -> 2169, the guard's own count; rls-smoke cases unchanged at 1087. Probe digests move for the pinned trigger, pinned grant and index coverage probes only. A later batch that adds a migration must regenerate pinned-grants.json and the known exceptions (their _how_measured names the last migration), and one that adds a trigger must pin it. The amendment paths stay three, so no open_blockers line pin moves.
known_limitations: The pinned trigger probe reads tables in app and private only; a trigger on a table in another schema is read by no rule here.
The export rule's token/credential half reads column NAMES (token, secret, credential, password; a *_redacted flag excepted); a material column named otherwise is the §5 cell's to class.
The audit-table tripwire is a text scan: a dynamic EXECUTE is not read; the catalog assertion for every role on either audit table stays owed with batch 141's migration (open_blockers[191] (9)).
A COPY whose words are computed at run time is not read by the lexer, as for client_encoding.
The pinned grant probe's rules 7 and 8, like 2-4, fail by design on a provisioned platform instance until Q170-c measures its roles, schema owners and default ACLs.

Left owed, outside this batch's list: C0 R2's other two guards and Q0 R-2 on 160-prep ([192]); Q0 R-1 and C0 R-1 on 170-assert ([193]); C0 N4's lint message ([191] (8)); A1 R3, R4 on 150-prereq ([194]); everything else those blockers and [185] hold.
open_risks_or_blockers: open_blockers[185] and [191]-[195] each record what this batch closed and what stays owed, with owners; none is stop-the-line.
